answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a meaningful stake in a shared vault before it may transact. Attackers must fund a separate stake for every fake identity, so forging a thousand accounts costs a thousand stakes while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues on a public ridge of verified work history, and newcomers start in a low-trust oasis where they can only earn small tasks until their stake-backed record proves them reliable.
